description: Printer paper and toner. Tax invoice, total includes GST $15.00.
explanation: A normal taxable purchase with a tax invoice: GST on Expenses claims the $15 at 1B.

description: Money out: monthly account keeping fee.
explanation: Bank fees are financial supplies with no GST charged, so there is nothing to claim: GST Free Expenses.

description: Business laptop, tax invoice, $2,499.00 including GST.
explanation: Equipment is a capital purchase: GST on Capital puts it in G10 and claims the GST at 1B.

description: October rent for the office. Tax invoice from a GST-registered landlord.
explanation: Commercial rent from a registered landlord is taxable. (Residential rent would be input-taxed.)

description: Money out: super contributions for the 6 October pay run.
explanation: Paying super clears the Superannuation Payable liability raised by payroll. Super is BAS excluded.

description: Money out: BAS payment for July–September (GST portion).
explanation: Paying the BAS clears the GST liability account. The payment itself has no GST.

description: Creative Cloud subscription. ABN supplied, invoice shows no Australian GST.
explanation: No GST was charged, so none can be claimed: GST Free Expenses. Coding it GST on Expenses would claim GST that was never paid.

description: Public liability insurance. Tax invoice shows GST of $120.00 on a total of $1,320.00.
explanation: General insurance is taxable; the invoice shows the GST. (Stamp duty on a premium, where shown separately, has no GST.)

description: Fuel for the business ute, $88.00 including GST.
explanation: Fuel is taxable. Claim only the business-use share if the vehicle is also used privately.

description: Lunch with a prospective client, $132.00 including GST.
explanation: Entertainment that is not income-tax deductible gives no GST credit. Many firms code it with no GST to claim; some use BAS Excluded. Check your firm's policy.

from: Your sales invoice to Coastline Cafe
description: Brand design work, $2,200.00 including GST.
explanation: A taxable sale: GST on Income reports $2,200 at G1 and $200 at 1A.

from: Your sales invoice to a Singapore customer
description: Goods shipped from Melbourne to Singapore within 60 days.
explanation: Exported goods are GST-free: G1 and G2, no 1A.

description: Money out: sole trader transfers $5,000 to their personal account.
explanation: Drawings are equity, not an expense, and are BAS excluded.

description: Money in: interest on the business savings account.
explanation: Interest is an input-taxed financial supply: it reports at G1 and G4 with no GST.

description: Domestic parcel postage, $22.00 including GST.
explanation: Domestic postage is taxable.

description: Stationery, £60.00 including VAT. VAT invoice.
explanation: A standard-rated purchase: £10 VAT reclaimed in box 4, £50 in box 7.

description: Money out: monthly business account charge.
explanation: Bank charges are exempt financial services: no VAT to reclaim. Some firms use No VAT instead.

description: Professional indemnity insurance, £540.00 including Insurance Premium Tax.
explanation: Insurance is exempt from VAT; IPT is not VAT and cannot be reclaimed.

description: Return train ticket London to Manchester for a client visit.
explanation: Passenger transport is zero-rated: box 7 only, no VAT to reclaim.

description: Dinner with two clients, £180.00 including VAT.
explanation: VAT on business entertainment of clients is blocked, so none is reclaimed. Many firms code it No VAT; others use a blocked-VAT rate. Check your firm's policy.

description: Laptop for a new employee, £1,199.00 including VAT.
explanation: Equipment with VAT: reclaim the £199.83 in box 4. Capitalise it if over the capitalisation policy.

description: Money out: business rates, October instalment.
explanation: Business rates are a local tax, outside the scope of VAT.

description: Money out: VAT return payment for the quarter to 31 August.
explanation: Paying HMRC clears the VAT control account; the payment is outside the scope.

description: Money out: net salaries for October.
explanation: The payroll journal already expensed gross pay; the bank payment clears Wages Payable. Payroll is outside the scope of VAT.

description: Plastering on a client's refurbishment, £4,000.00 net. Invoice says "reverse charge: customer to account for VAT to HMRC". VAT registered, CIS verified.
explanation: Construction services under CIS between VAT-registered businesses, and you are not the end user: the domestic reverse charge applies. Boxes 1, 4 and 7.

from: Your sales invoice to Northwind Ltd
description: Consultancy, £2,400.00 including VAT.
explanation: A standard-rated sale: £400 in box 1, £2,000 in box 6.

from: Your sales invoice to a school
description: Printed books, £300.00.
explanation: Printed books are zero-rated: box 6 only.

description: First class stamps (universal service).
explanation: Royal Mail universal service postage is exempt from VAT.

description: Money in: interest on the business deposit account.
explanation: Interest received is an exempt financial supply: box 6 only. Some firms use No VAT.
